name: httpx — published Python HTTP client library
description: Published Python HTTP client. Benchmark target is actual ACIMA module ownership, not internal component discovery.
softwareCategory: Reusable HTTP client library (PUBLISHED; no application or service host)
architectureFamily: Layered library with an explicit transport interface and interchangeable default, ASGI, WSGI and mock transports
expectedCharacteristics: Installable package declared in pyproject.toml with a public re-export surface in httpx/__init__.py
Client and request API layer in httpx/_client.py and httpx/_api.py
Transport seam in httpx/_transports: an abstract interface plus concrete transports
Shared request/response models in httpx/_models.py and URL handling in httpx/_urls.py
No application entry point, dependency-injection container or deployment topology
Lint and type checking plus a test workflow, but no architecture dependency rules
profileNotes: The library profile would be the natural fit for a published surface, but it is implemented only by the TypeScript and .NET reference enforcers in this ACIMA revision. Asserting the profile here would claim enforcement that does not exist.

expectedBoundaries.rationale: The prior operator-reviewed ACIMA unit map declares httpx/ as one implementation module. Internal API/client/transport/model/auth/content areas are components, not independently adjudicated ACIMA modules. Reviewers may challenge this reference only with evidence against explicit contracts, implementation ownership, dependency isolation, data/configuration ownership, and controlled composition.

expectedObservations.statement: There is no ACIMA unit map or enforcer in the repository, so a base-profile assessment begins at NEEDS_UNIT_MAP rather than at a conformance claim.
The library profile is not implemented for Python, so the published public surface cannot be classified by this revision's enforcer.
Existing automation covers linting, type checking and tests, not architectural dependency rules.
The transport layer has an explicit interface and interchangeable implementations, a component-level port/adapter seam; this alone does not establish a separate ACIMA module ownership boundary.

knownLimitations: No violation-level ground truth is recorded for this scenario, so finding precision and recall are reported unavailable rather than estimated.
The unit-map a correct assessment proposes is not unique; several defensible maps exist.
httpx does not run the ACIMA enforcer on itself, so no independent finding set exists to compare against.
Java and .NET are irrelevant here; Python coverage includes 41 automated rules and 14 manual-evidence rules.

groundTruth.method: Manual inspection of the pinned checkout and prior operator-reviewed ACIMA unit map benchmark-evidence/rw-2026-11-08-02/configs/httpx.acima.config.json, which declares one implementation module covering httpx/. The map is a reference hypothesis requiring independent qualitative review.
groundTruth.notes: Benchmark target is ACIMA module ownership. Component discovery is supporting evidence only. The one-module reference is author-adjudicated and has not received independent second-reviewer adjudication.

ownershipEvidence: dependency isolation and permitted dependency edges
boundaryMeasurement.rule: A candidate is not an ACIMA module solely because it has a name, directory, package, class, interface, or distinct responsibility.
